rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round pushes obfuscation intensity up across the board while keeping cost-sensitivity weights low, since the binary is tiny (190 bytes of text, largest function only 109 bytes) and can absorb size/runtime growth cheaply. SUB, BCF, and IBR get the highest SecurityGain weights to target the arithmetic and control-flow of main and the small True/False::and_m methods, where static pattern-matching is the main reverse-engineering vector; ICALL and IGV are weighted strongly on DiversityGain to convert direct calls and globals into indirected forms, adding structural variance across the four functions without meaningfully bloating a 190-byte text section. FLA is kept moderately aggressive on main but tempered on CorrectnessRisk since flattening the recursive benchmark logic is the likeliest source of subtle behavioral breakage; SPLIT is intentionally left weak because the functions are too small for basic-block splitting to add real resistance, so its budget stays low to avoid wasting transforms on noise.
